clue.text: Told to pay for book following step-by-step instructions

indicators.note: something told is spoken, so the word for paying is taken by its sound

parts.note: to pay for something is to buy it
Numbers is the fourth book of the Old Testament

explanation.surface: Someone is instructed to pay for a book, perhaps a manual of step-by-step instructions.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something by numbers means doing it mechanically, one prescribed step after another, like painting by numbers.

clue.text: Group of unmissable, up-and-coming singers

indicators.note: in a down clue coming up means reading from bottom to top, backwards
a group of the letters of unmissable is hidden within that word

parts.note: the word unmissable holds the singers' name inside it, read in reverse

explanation.surface: A band of rising young vocalists is not to be missed.
explanation.definitionFit: Bassi is a plural of basso, a bass singer, the lowest male voice.

clue.text: Nothing being required, polite refusal's a customary practice

parts.note: no, ta is a polite way to decline, ta being British for thanks; the 's is added
taken as written
usage is established custom

explanation.surface: If nothing is needed, declining politely is the done thing.
explanation.walkthrough: Ta is informal British for thank you.
explanation.definitionFit: Not a sausage is British slang for nothing at all, as in we got not a sausage.

clue.text: Butterfly to be seen during spring month

indicators.note: something happening during a period sits inside it

parts.note: March falls in spring in the northern hemisphere
a thing that is on is showing, on display

explanation.surface: A butterfly can be spotted in early spring.
explanation.definitionFit: The monarch is a large orange and black migratory butterfly of North America.

clue.text: Mezzanine floor in French store left in disarray

parts.note: en is French for in

indicators.note: letters in disarray are muddled into a new arrangement

parts.note: the word store is used as written, its letters mixed with the L

explanation.surface: A shop in France has its mezzanine left untidy.
explanation.definitionFit: An entresol is a low storey between ground and first floor, the same as a mezzanine.

clue.text: On board vessel, trap squirming fish

indicators.note: something on board is inside the ship, between the letters for the vessel

parts.note: SS stands for steamship

indicators.note: squirming letters wriggle into a new order

parts.note: the word trap is used as written, its letters wriggled about

explanation.surface: On a boat, a trap is full of wriggling fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprats are small herring-like sea fish; fish works as a plural noun.

clue.text: Bills inscribed with American president's name

indicators.note: a thing inscribed with a word has that word written within it, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: bills are advertisements, ADS for short

explanation.surface: Banknotes or posters carry the printed name of a US president.
explanation.definitionFit: John Adams and John Quincy Adams were both presidents of the United States, so this surname belongs to two of them.

clue.text: Track heading off north of solitary location in Ireland

indicators.note: in a down clue, north of means placed above, so earlier
the word for track has its first letter taken off

parts.note: a path is a track
lone means solitary

explanation.surface: A track heads away north from a remote spot in Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Athlone is a town on the River Shannon in the middle of Ireland.

clue.text: A silver-headed commander

indicators.note: headed by silver means the silver symbol comes at the top

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
taken as written

explanation.surface: An officer with grey or white hair.
explanation.walkthrough: Silver-headed reads as grey-haired, but it says silver goes at the head.
explanation.definitionFit: An aga is a Turkish military commander or chief officer in the Ottoman Empire.

clue.text: Hidden among cast, top performer's denied lead

indicators.note: being among something means sitting inside it

parts.note: to cast is to shed, as a snake casts its skin

indicators.note: a word denied its lead loses its first letter

parts.note: a belter is an outstanding performer or performance; the 's is is

explanation.surface: A star actor's name is concealed within the cast list, left without the lead role.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sheltered is screened or protected from view, which makes it hidden.

clue.text: Fail to deal with youngster drinking vermouth

indicators.note: one who drinks takes the liquid in, so the drink goes inside the drinker

parts.note: a son is a young male child
IT is short for Italian vermouth, as in gin and it

explanation.surface: Someone neglects a problem with a young person who has been drinking vermouth.
explanation.walkthrough: Gin and it is a British cocktail of gin and Italian (sweet) vermouth, hence IT.
explanation.definitionFit: To sit on a complaint or a report is to delay acting on it, deliberately leaving it unaddressed.

clue.text: Competition in part of Europe to capture sea monster

indicators.note: capturing something holds it inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: Thrace is a region of south-east Europe split between Greece, Bulgaria and Turkey
an orc is a sea monster in old literature, such as Ariosto's

explanation.surface: A contest held in a European region to catch a monster of the deep.
explanation.walkthrough: The orc here is the sea monster of old literature, not Tolkien's goblin; it was also an old name for the killer whale.
explanation.definitionFit: A torch race was an ancient Greek relay contest in which runners passed on a lit torch, so it is a kind of competition.

clue.text: Revolting type shaken up by restriction in US

definitions.note: a revolting person is one in revolt, not a disgusting one

indicators.note: letters shaken up are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: these three words are used as written, all of their letters reshuffled

explanation.surface: A disgusting character is rattled by some American restriction.
explanation.walkthrough: Revolting looks like disgusting, but it means rising in revolt.
explanation.definitionFit: An insurrectionist takes part in an uprising against authority, the literal sense of someone who is revolting.

clue.text: Praise Monet, working to be an impressionist

indicators.note: letters working are being worked over into a new arrangement

parts.note: these two words are used as written, all their letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Praising Monet at work seems to make one an Impressionist painter.
explanation.walkthrough: Monet points to Impressionist painting, but the impressionist is a mimic.
explanation.definitionFit: An impressionist is an entertainer who mimics people, which is to impersonate them.

clue.text: Money given to kid for dumpling

parts.note: dough is slang for money
a kid is a child, here a boy

explanation.surface: Cash handed to a child to buy a dumpling.
explanation.definitionFit: A doughboy is a boiled or fried dumpling, a name used in Britain and the Caribbean as well as for a US soldier.

clue.text: Knight I put on board, lacking certainty

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece put on another is placed above it

parts.note: to dub is to make someone a knight with a tap of the sword
taken as written
a table is a board, as in board and lodging

explanation.surface: A chess knight placed on the board, its future unsure.
explanation.walkthrough: Knight looks like a noun, but it is read as the verb to knight.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dubitable can be doubted, open to question, so it is uncertain.

clue.text: Stingy type returns material for electronic device

parts.note: a bee is a creature that stings, read literally rather than as mean

indicators.note: returning means the word for material is read backwards

parts.note: rep is a ribbed fabric

explanation.surface: A miser sends back fabric meant for a gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: Stingy looks like miserly, but it is read as able to sting.
explanation.definitionFit: A beeper is a small electronic pager that bleeps to alert its wearer.

clue.text: The going rate for high-fliers?

definitions.meaning: normally the usual price, here read as the speed of travel
high-fliers are usually high achievers, here aircraft

explanation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like a pay scale for executives.
explanation.definitionFit: Airspeed is an aircraft's speed relative to the air around it, how fast flying craft go.

clue.text: Mark time as political leader, once

parts.note: a brand is an identifying mark burned or stamped on

explanation.surface: Someone marks time in the role of a former politician.
explanation.walkthrough: Mark time looks like a single phrase, but the words work separately.
explanation.definitionFit: Willy Brandt was Chancellor of West Germany from 1969 to 1974, a past head of government.

clue.text: Cover up novel problem

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a lid is a cover
Emma is a novel by Jane Austen

explanation.surface: Someone hushes up a new problem.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilemma is a difficult situation with no clearly good choice, a kind of problem.

clue.text: Danced round about, getting confounded

indicators.note: round says the dancing word goes around the word for about

parts.note: to jig is to dance a lively jig
about gives RE, which turns round to ER as the clue's round about suggests

explanation.surface: Someone who danced around in circles ends up utterly bewildered.
explanation.walkthrough: The usual short word for about is read the wrong way round, as round about hints.
explanation.definitionFit: Jiggered is British slang for exhausted or confounded, as in 'I'll be jiggered'.

clue.text: Incoherent speaker given Ibsen role for reading aloud

indicators.note: read aloud means the role's name is judged by how it sounds

parts.note: Hedda Gabler is the title role of Ibsen's play

explanation.surface: An actor who mumbles is given an Ibsen part to read through.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent, where the R is not pronounced, the two words sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A garbler is someone who jumbles their words so they cannot be understood.

clue.text: No good dodging service, anyway

indicators.note: one who dodges stays out, so these letters are taken out

parts.note: evensong is the Anglican evening service

explanation.surface: It's no good trying to skip church; you'll go regardless.
explanation.definitionFit: Even so means nevertheless, in spite of that, much as anyway does.

clue.text: Indication that fight's to begin, with a show of hands?

definitions.meaning: the idiom announces that a contest will now be fought without restraint
taken literally, removing boxing gloves shows the bare hands

explanation.walkthrough: A show of hands sounds like a vote, but here it is boxers baring their fists.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom signals that a dispute will now be conducted ruthlessly, as in a bare-knuckle bout.

clue.text: Evil, though upstanding in the end

indicators.note: in a down clue, standing up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: sin is evil
if can mean though, as in rich if dull

explanation.surface: Wickedness, even if respectable at last.
explanation.walkthrough: Upstanding looks like honest, but it means standing upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Finis is Latin for end, printed at the close of a book or film.

clue.text: Brummel — name that's in fashion for society types

parts.note: Beau Brummell was the Regency dandy, so his nickname stands for him

indicators.note: the name letter is in the fashion word, sitting inside it

parts.note: mode is a fashion or style

explanation.surface: The famous dandy's name is the one in vogue among high society.
explanation.walkthrough: Beau Brummell was the arbiter of men's fashion in Regency London.
explanation.definitionFit: The beau monde is fashionable high society, the people of the smart world.

clue.text: Play Man City regularly

indicators.note: regular letters are every other letter, here the second, fourth and sixth

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of these words are taken

explanation.surface: Manchester City play consistently.
explanation.walkthrough: Man City is Manchester City football club.
explanation.definitionFit: To act is to perform or play a part.

clue.text: Succeed in school, giving attention between start and end of lesson

indicators.note: one piece goes between the two others
only the first and last letters of the word lesson are used

parts.note: only the first and last letters of this word are kept, either side of the inserted piece
to give an ear is to pay attention

explanation.surface: Doing well at school means listening attentively throughout every lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: To learn is to acquire knowledge, which is what succeeding at school amounts to.

clue.text: Baxter didn't start out as a small-time actor

indicators.note: out here means wrong or disordered, so the letters are rearranged
a word that did not start loses its first letter

parts.note: the surname is used as written, then loses its first letter

explanation.surface: An actor called Baxter began his career with minor parts.
explanation.definitionFit: An extra is a performer hired for a crowd scene with no lines, the lowest rung of acting.

clue.text: Like soldiers without commander in mess?

definitions.meaning: troops with nobody to command them receive no orders
a mess is also the soldiers' dining hall, and the answer means disordered

explanation.walkthrough: Mess suggests the military dining room; it is the untidy kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Something orderless is without order or arrangement, chaotic, like a squad given no orders.
